explanation: File system level (gateway/AMS) ransomware detection -- confirmed via a real product QA test spec (2026-08-27) as a genuinely separate mechanism from both the plain ransomware entry (rChecker/RefCopy) and system binary/library tampering. The /athinio/bin/oneCloudFilerx binary itself detects mass file overwrite/change activity (per the test case: overwriting/changing more than 500 files within a 1-hour window) and updates /athinio/security/config.xml's <RansomDetected> tag to 'YES'. /athinio/bin/gatewayMonitor.sh reads that config.xml and sets /athinio/system/alertlog.xml's <AMS_Ransom_current_status> to 1, which then rolls up directly to Alert.xml's amsrans tag.

metadata.writer_script: /athinio/bin/oneCloudFilerx (mass file-change detection, >500 files/hour) -> /athinio/security/config.xml's RansomDetected -> /athinio/bin/gatewayMonitor.sh -> athinio/system/alertlog.xml's AMS_Ransom_current_status, rolling up to Alert.xml's amsrans
metadata.confidence: verified -- confirmed against a real product QA test spec; amsrans/AMS_Ransom_current_status both confirmed present and reading 0 (clean) on a real hierarchy

value_meanings.0: Clean -- oneCloudFilerx has not observed mass file overwrite/change activity (the documented threshold is >500 files changed within a 1-hour window) since the last reset. Confirmed live on real hierarchy 5/101/1/4/1 (2026-08-27).
value_meanings.1: File-system-level ransomware detected -- more than 500 files were overwritten or changed within a 1-hour window, matching a mass-encryption/mass-corruption pattern rather than an isolated file modification.

metadata.caveat: requires_live_recompute (not diffable/readable-report) because the underlying trigger is a rolling activity-volume threshold inside a compiled binary (oneCloudFilerx), not a static file this workflow can independently re-derive from a snapshot -- verification would require re-running the actual detection, not comparing files. This is distinct from the plain 'ransomware' attack type (Ransom/bin/lib, based on rChecker's RefCopy diff and Alert1.sh's binary/library modification checks) -- oneCloudFilerx's file-count-based mechanism is a separate gateway-specific detector, even though both ultimately mean 'files are being mass-tampered with'.
